label: Commun (appliqué à tous les thèmes)
_comment: Applied to every flow (text API and documents), with and without theme.

PaymentCardNumberRecognizer, AnyDomainEmailRecognizer and the NIR (EXT-08, EXT-23) were on the text routes only (app/themes/extension/identifiers.json, D-015) until phase 2; moved here by decision Q4 of 2026-10-04.
include_theme_recognizers reuses a theme's recognizer by name instead of copying its regex (no duplication, no drift); an unknown name fails startup.

patterns.name: adresse postale française (numéro + type de voie + nom de rue), suivie le cas échéant du code postal et de la ville sur la même ligne, après une virgule ou à la ligne suivante (EXT-29)
initiale(s) + nom de famille (ex: J-M. Costa, S. Haim-Boukobza, A. Amara Petitjean)

payment card number, same regex as Presidio 2.2.364 CreditCardRecognizer (predefined_recognizers/generic/credit_card_recognizer.py, registered for 'en' only, EXT-08); no Luhn check possible in an ad hoc recognizer: false positives accepted (doctrine 0.1), measured; score 0.6 keeps a margin above every threshold (0.4 everywhere, code default included since EXT-15 was fixed in phase 2)

payment card number written one digit at a time with a single separator between digits (EXT-30: '4 9 7 0 ...' was never detected, the regex above expects groups); 13 to 19 digits, same leading digits as above; a 15-digit sequence starting with 1 or 2 has the NIR shape and is left to the NIR recognizer
email address with any domain, including internal ones (.local, .lan, .internal) rejected by Presidio's EmailRecognizer TLD check (EXT-23); simplified dot-atom addr-spec (RFC 5322 s.3.4.1)

postal code followed by a capitalized city name, alone or after a street (EXT-29: '21000 Dijon' was left in clear next to its detected street, 12 of 24 addresses partly exposed in the base variant, phase 1); metropolitan departments 01-95 and overseas 97-98 (98 included for Monaco and the Pacific), Corsica 2A/2B; case-sensitive initial (?-i:) because presidio compiles with IGNORECASE, so that '12345 euros' or '75011 en attente' do not match

IBAN with any or no single separator between characters (EXT-30: 'F R 2 9 7 5 ...' one character at a time was partly exposed, Presidio's IbanRecognizer expects groups of 4); ISO 13616 shape: 2 upper-case letters, 2 check digits, 11 to 30 upper-case letters or digits; no checksum possible in an ad hoc recognizer (false positives accepted, doctrine 0.1); letters case-sensitive (?-i:) so that ordinary words do not start a match

French date with the month in letters, optional weekday, '1er', abbreviated months, optional year (EXT-31: '14 mai 1981' was never detected, 25 dates exposed out of 71 in phase 1); a day number is required so that 'mars' or 'mai' alone never match

English date with the month in letters: 'March 3, 2025', 'Monday, March 3, 2025', '3rd of March 2025', '3 March 2025' (EXT-31; the analyzer always runs in French, EXT-19, so English dates in prompts were missed); abbreviations need their dot ('Jan' alone is a first name) and a day number is required ('May I help' does not match)
